title: Blog Review: Oct. 28
gist: Semiconductor Engineering's Oct. 28 blog roundup: large-format and curvilinear masks, STCO for chiplets, physical AI co-design, verification of AI-generated RTL, and scale-up fabrics, plus process-side posts on CFET, integrated voltage regulators and photonics test. A link digest with thin detail.

insights.claim: An eBeam Initiative expert panel covered large-format masks, equipment investment, high-NA EUV and curvilinear masks as current mask-industry topics.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Watch mask-writer and high-NA EUV ecosystem investment.

themes.theme: Heterogeneous design and AI in design flows

insights.claim: Siemens says the shift to chiplet-based and heterogeneous design makes system technology co-optimization and multiphysics analysis essential for thermal, power and integration bottlenecks.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Supports demand for multiphysics EDA tools tied to 3D-IC.

insights.claim: Cadence argues that as AI can generate RTL, propose ECOs, modify constraints and create verification properties, confirming the resulting design still meets requirements matters more than ever.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Verification and sign-off tooling gains importance as design generation is automated.

insights.claim: Arm describes an evidence-first harness engineering approach combining indexed workload data, bounded LLM analysis and simulation evidence for source-less microarchitectural analysis.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Example of bounded LLM use in CPU performance work.

insights.claim: Synopsys argues physical AI systems need a new engineering form that co-designs and validates silicon, sensors, software, mechanics and power using a holistic physics-aware approach.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Physical AI broadens EDA scope into system-level co-design.

insights.claim: Keysight says tensor parallelism is the first parallelism dimension any scale-up fabric, whether NVLink or Ethernet, must get right.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Scale-up fabric benchmarks should be judged on tensor-parallel performance first.
insights.quote: tensor parallelism is the first parallelism dimension that any scale-up fabric, whether it’s NVLink or Ethernet, must get right

insights.claim: Lam Research presents a self-aligned CFET process sequence for SRAM and logic that gains performance through larger effective channel width and improved electrostatics at smaller nodes.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: CFET process maturity is a leading indicator for post-nanosheet scaling toolsets.

insights.claim: Intel Foundry says integrated voltage regulators reduce current density, provide higher regulation bandwidth and reduce reliance on large decoupling capacitor networks.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen

insights.claim: SEMI identified seven themes shaping MEMS and sensors, with robotics and medical bringing new requirements and opportunities for differentiation.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Robotics and medical are flagged as MEMS demand drivers.

insights.claim: Advantest outlines new photonics test requirements: fiber alignment, coupling efficiency, polarization management and optical instrumentation.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Silicon-photonics growth creates new ATE demand.
